agent_summary:
Tested the session-management lane against OWASP Juice Shop at http://juice.lab.test (nginx→Express). Findings by item:

SESS-01 (schema, done): Session is a stateless RS256 bearer JWT, not a server session. whoami is empty anonymous (x2) and returns the caller identity with a session (sess1=id39 x3/x46, sess2=id40 x14/x100, athn1 x112). package.json (x12) pins jsonwebtoken/express-jwt and /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub (x8) exposes the RS256 public key. Auth and role are both read from the token: customer endpoints 401 anon (x33/x34/x24/x22), admin-only /rest/order-history/orders is 403 to a customer (x36).

SESS-02 (cookie attributes, done): No server response sets a session cookie — GET / (x1) and authenticated GET /profile (x16) carry no Set-Cookie; the login POST (x7) delivers the JWT in the JSON body. The token therefore lives in localStorage / a client-set cookie with no server-enforced HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite.

SESS-03 (fixation, N/A): No server-set session identifier exists to fix; a fresh JWT is minted at login.

SESS-04 (exposed session variables, done): Access log is exposed (x11) but shows no tokens in URLs (auth via body/Authorization header). However session-equivalent secrets leak: deluxeToken/totpSecret of other users via unauthenticated /rest/memories (x20) and via /rest/user/authentication-details to any customer (x5/x89).

SESS-05 (CSRF, done + lead): The server-rendered /profile page (x16/x17) has three state-changing POST forms (username, image URL, image file) with no anti-CSRF token, and there is no SameSite session cookie. Recorded as a medium lead (not submitted).

SESS-06 (logout, done): No server-side logout — GET /rest/user/logout returns 500 "Unexpected path" (x18) and the SPA bundle (x9) references no logout route; a captured JWT stays valid until expiry.

SESS-07 (timeout, OPEN): The JWT's exp/idle lifetime could not be measured because the gateway injects the bearer token and never exposes it to this run; app config (x13) exposes no timeout and the stateless design has no server-side invalidation. Recommend a reviewer with a real token decode its exp claim.

SESS-08 (puzzling, N/A): No server-side session store; auth state is wholly in the signed JWT, so there are no cross-workflow session variables to puzzle.

SESS-09 (hijacking, done + high lead): Token forgery/theft exposure — RS256 public key downloadable (x8) with the legacy jsonwebtoken stack (x12), other users' tokens leaked (x20/x5), no HttpOnly server cookie, no server-side invalidation (x18), and wildcard CORS returns ACAO:* even to a hostile Origin on authenticated whoami (x107/x108).

Coverage: ~123 requests across the real surface (REST/API, /profile, /ftp + /encryptionkeys + /support/logs listings and files, /metrics, config, static assets). Reachable paths include /rest/user/whoami, /rest/user/authentication-details, /rest/memories, /rest/2fa/status, /rest/wallet/balance, /api/Users(+/{id}), /api/Cards, /api/Addresss, /api/Complaints, /rest/basket/{id}, /api/Products(+/{id}), /rest/products/{id}/reviews, /rest/admin/application-configuration, /metrics, /ftp/*, /encryptionkeys/*, /support/logs/*. I also corroborated the cross-lane BOLA issues (any customer session reads /api/Users, /api/Users/{id}, and foreign /rest/basket/{id}; /api/Quantitys readable), already reported by other lanes. Writes were limited to registering one throwaway account (x6) and logging it in (x7) under the approved lab write rules; no destructive actions. Note bodies were not displayed after the run's display budget was exhausted mid-run, but all responses are retained as evidence.

leads.title: [agent] Session JWT forgeable/stealable: RS256 public key exposed, session tokens leaked, no HttpOnly, wildcard CORS

detail.text: Session hijacking exposure: (1) /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub (x8) exposes the RS256 public key and package.json (x12) pins the old jsonwebtoken/express-jwt stack whose signing private key is bundled in Juice Shop source, enabling token forgery. (2) deluxeToken/totpSecret of other users are readable unauthenticated via /rest/memories (x20) and by any customer via /rest/user/authentication-details (x5). (3) The token is not protected by an HttpOnly server cookie (no Set-Cookie on any response, x1/x16) and every response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * , so an XSS or malicious origin can read the token from localStorage/cookie. There is no server-side logout/invalidation (x18), so a captured JWT stays valid until expiry. For a reviewer to validate token forgery/replay.

leads.title: [agent] State-changing /profile forms lack anti-CSRF tokens; JWT also accepted from non-SameSite cookie

detail.text: The server-rendered authenticated page GET /profile (exchanges x16/x17, as sess1) contains three POST forms — ./profile (username change), ./profile/image/url (imageUrl), and ./profile/image/file (file upload) — none of which carry a hidden anti-CSRF token. No server response sets a SameSite-scoped session cookie (x1, x16 have no Set-Cookie), and Juice Shop reads the JWT from a client-set 'token' cookie, so these authenticated state changes can be driven cross-site. Not submitted (writes require approval); reported as observed form structure.

items.na_reason: [agent] App uses stateless bearer-JWT auth with no server-set session identifier (no Set-Cookie on any response); there is no pre-auth session token that survives login to fix, so session fixation does not apply.

[agent] No server-side session store exists; authentication state is entirely within the signed JWT, so there are no shared/overloaded session variables across workflows to puzzle. Not applicable to this stateless design.
